_findings: The PP-DocLayout-V3 fix (plugin 0.2.4) works: with RapidOCR, scanned-page text goes from 2 % to 100 %, synthetic ground-truth F1 from 0.84 to 0.95, the handwritten note and the phone photo from empty to readable; born-digital documents are unchanged (text-layer recall 0.825 → 0.828).

For printed and born-digital documents RapidOCR is the right default: the same quality as GLM-OCR on the synthetic set (F1 0.96 vs 0.94) at a sixteenth of the time (170 s vs 2'745 s for all 28 documents).

GLM-OCR is far better on handwriting and photos: 97 % of the handwritten note (RapidOCR 27–31 %) and 85 % of the phone photo's handwriting with the default layout (RapidOCR 11–30 %). Its misreadings can change the meaning ("FORCED AND NATURAL"); check the "Words not in reference" tab.

GLM-OCR plugin bug (docling-glm-ocr): when docling finds nothing to OCR on a page, the plugin OCRs the whole page instead. Every born-digital page goes to the VLM (CELEX: 1'791 s vs 92 s with RapidOCR; 5 of 5 probed pages sent as full-page crops) and the extra OCR text lowers precision against the text layer (0.82 vs 0.92).

PP-DocLayout-V3 recovers more real text than docling's default layout (text-layer recall 0.83 vs 0.75, e.g. labels on the architectural plans that the default layout treats as one picture) but finds fewer headings on the synthetic set (0.85 vs 1.00). With GLM-OCR on the phone photo its regions fragment the handwriting (22 % vs 85 % with the default layout).
Before the fix, GLM-OCR + PP-DocLayout-V3 looked fine on scans only because of the GLM-OCR full-page fallback covering for the layout plugin bug.

cons: 16× slower than RapidOCR (2'745 s, 1.87 s per page): the plugin sends every page without OCR regions to the VLM as a full page.
Lower precision against the text layer (0.82 vs 0.92) and VLM misreadings that can change the meaning.
pros: Handwritten note 97 %, phone photo 85 % handwriting and 100 % printed text.
Synthetic set close to RapidOCR (F1 0.94, scanned page 0.96).
fixed-glm.verdict: Best for handwriting and photos; do not use on born-digital documents until the plugin's full-page fallback is fixed.

cons: Phone photo handwriting drops to 22 %: PP-DocLayout-V3 regions fragment the handwriting before GLM-OCR reads it.
Same full-page fallback cost as GLM-OCR with the default layout (2'792 s).
pros: Text-layer recall 0.83 (layout finds the plan labels); handwritten note 97 %.
fixed-glm-pp.verdict: No advantage over GLM-OCR with the default layout on photos; same speed problem.

cons: Handwriting: 31 % of the handwritten note, 30 % of the phone photo's handwriting, none of the printed letterhead on the photo.
The default layout treats most of the architectural plans as one picture (three of five come out empty), so their text is missing (text-layer recall 0.75).
pros: Fastest configuration: 170 s for all 28 documents, 0.24 s per page (CELEX in 92 s).
Synthetic set: F1 0.96, tables 1.00, headings 1.00, scanned page 0.99, text in screenshots 1.00.
fixed-rapidocr.verdict: Fast, complete default for printed documents; weak on handwriting.

cons: Fewer headings on the synthetic set (0.85 vs 1.00 with the default layout).
pros: Best text-layer recall together with GLM-OCR + PP (0.83) at RapidOCR speed (189 s, 0.23 s per page).
Scanned page 1.00, text in screenshots 1.00; recovers the letterhead on the phone photo (50 %).
fixed-rapidocr-pp.verdict: Recommended for printed documents with plans, charts or complex layouts.

cons: Same speed problem as the fixed GLM-OCR runs (2'760 s).
Text in screenshots and outlined text drop (0.75, 0.02) because the layout plugin still discards regions without PDF text.
pros: Scanned page 1.00, handwritten note 96 %, phone photo 81 % handwriting.
released-glm-pp.verdict: Looked fine on scans only because GLM-OCR's full-page fallback hid the layout bug.

cons: Scanned and image-only pages come out empty: synthetic scan 2 %, handwritten note and phone photo 0 words, Offerte page 4 empty.
released-rapidocr-pp.verdict: Broken on scans and images (plugin 0.2.3): shown for comparison only.
